# Autodisk

Basically a mashup of `Hyperdrive` and `Autobase`. It lets multiple people write to the same file system at the same time.

## What it does

- Feels just like normal Hyperdrive (`put`, `get`, `list`).
- Multiple devices can collaborate without stepping on each other's toes thanks to Autobase.
- You can easily share the disk key (`drive.base.key`, the autobase key) so friends can hop in.
- Automatically handles any messy conflicts for you.

## Usage

```javascript
const autodisk = require('autodisk')
const Corestore = require('corestore')

const store = new Corestore('./storage')

// Create a new autodisk
const drive = autodisk({ store })
await drive.ready()

// Join an existing autodisk (existing_key = drive.base.key of the other device)
const drive = autodisk({ store, bootstrap: existing_key })
await drive.ready()

// Write to the drive
await drive.put('/hello.txt', Buffer.from('Hello world!'))

// Read from the drive
const content = await drive.get('/hello.txt')
console.log(content.toString())

// Add a writer to collaborate
await drive.add_writer(peer_writer_key)
```

## Things to know

- The drive (its `db` and `blobs`) is built as autobase views, so every device gets the same drive key and hashes. How disks move forward and what gets pinned is in [docs/disks.md](../../../docs/disks.md).
- `list(folder)` gives the paths in that folder (not recursive unless `{ recursive: true }`), not a stream.
- Also there are `del`, `entry`, `exists`, `download`, `remove_writer` (removing the last indexer is skipped), `add_reader` / `remove_reader` / `get_readers` / `is_reader` (only a list, it doesnt control who can read), `get_writers` / `is_writer`, `on('update')`, `replicate`.
- Every `put` puts the whole file (base64) into the writers own autobase core, and again into `blobs`, so files are stored twice.
- The writer and reader lists are plain sets filled while `apply` runs, not a view, so autobase cant undo them when it reorders.
